title: Change control playbook for production model rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: define a prescriptive change-control playbook for model lifecycle operations (canary rollouts, A/B tests, shadow traffic, auto-rollback) that enforces RBAC, required sign-offs, and tamper-evident audit logs. The playbook should be implementable in the Redwood Console rollout UI and via API, and cover: rollout tiers, approval sequences, minimum telemetry baselines, rollback conditions, escalation paths, and log retention requirements. Goals: 1) Prevent accidental production degradation by formalizing who can start/stop/promote rollouts. 2) Make every production change auditable and reversible. 3) Minimize friction for low-risk changes while requiring strict controls for high-risk model updates.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC roles defined and mapped to Console actions (create rollout, promote, abort, change policy)
Console enforces pre-promotion sign-offs for high-risk rollouts and records signer identity in audit log
Audit logs capture before/after model versions, rollout percentages over time, metric snapshots, and user IDs; logs are exportable to customer KMS-integrated storage
Auto-rollback rules implementable by SLO thresholds and observable in the rollout UI with simulated dry-run
Playbook doc and a one-page cheat sheet published in Confluence; linkable from the rollout modal
